When atoms absorb light, they absorb radiation only at frequencies close to their natural oscillation frequencies, similar to traditional resonance in classical systems. Consequently, it carries away part of the energy, thereby reducing the energy of the emitted gamma quantum. Thus, gamma radiation emitted by a nucleus is not absorbed by another similar nucleus. R. Mössbauer showed that in some cases gamma quantum emission can occur without recoil, so that similar nuclei in similar conditions can strongly (resonantly) absorb this radiation.
